The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with the street grid turned about 14 degrees from true north. Adjoining sheets are 39 and 40 below, and further sheets lie to the right.
notes: The previous-edition sheet number printed under the sheet number is cut off in the binding gutter.
A street name at the left edge, partly lost in the gutter, appears to read N. 7th St.; it was not used.

Placed only from the junctions of Erie Street with North 8th Street and North 9th Street, hand-picked from the drawn water-pipe corners; both lie along one street, so the placement is a two-point fit.
Almost the whole sheet is open ground or river, so there is very little line work to check the fit against.
printed sheet 45, 50 ft: N 8th and N 9th to the river, city playground; two points on Erie, low confidence

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 covers the Camden ferry and railroad terminal on the Delaware River between Erie Street at the top and the coal yard at the bottom. The streets on the right of the sheet are Beach Street, running down from Erie Street through North Street and York Street, and Delaware Avenue, which leaves York Street on a long diagonal and carries on to State Street. Wood Street crosses between them. The big building on the shore is the Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad) ferry house and freight depot, with the Shackamaxon Ferry and Vine Street Ferry slips and waiting room inside it, the offices and a separate freight depot beside it. Next to it are the Blair Housewrecking and Salvage Co. yard, a wood sawing shed, storage sheds and a wagon shed. South of the ferry house the sheet is filled by the terminal's tracks, which fan out from the ferry house toward the lower right. In the lower left are a further slip, a tool house and the wharf and yard of H. V. Vaughan Son & Co., wharf and bridge builders, with a wooden pier and a coal trestle. The Delaware River and the ferry slips fill the left of the sheet, with a compass rose at the upper left. Water pipes and street widths of 50 ft are lettered in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with the street grid turned about 14 degrees from true north. Adjoining sheets are 41 above, 35 to the right and 47 below.
notes: Previous edition: sheet 23 of volume 1, printed under the sheet number.

Placed by a two-point fit on Delaware Avenue at York Street (detected) and Delaware Avenue at State Street (hand-picked at the pipe corner); the track yard and ferry house have no surviving street junctions.
Beach Street and Wood Street are not in OpenStreetMap; the Beach Street / York Street corner agrees with sheet 35's placement to about 2 m.
The ferry terminal, the ferry slips and the track yard no longer exist; this is the area of the Ben Franklin Bridge plaza and the modern waterfront.
printed sheet 46, 50 ft: PRR ferry house and terminal tracks; two points, low confidence

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows the Camden waterfront in the lumber and paper district between Vine Street at the top and Linden Street near the bottom, along the Delaware River and Delaware Avenue. Delaware Avenue, which runs down the right side of the sheet, is the only through street. Vine Street and Elm Street (marked not opened) run west from it toward the river, and Linden Street and Pearl Street are lettered near the bottom right. Most of the ground is lumber yards: the Chas. Stockham Saw Mill and Lumber Yard with a sawing and planing mill, the West Jersey Paper Mfg. Co. with a paper mill and storage, the Munger & Bennett Lumber Yard and the David Baird lumber, spars and piling yard, each with sheds, piles of lumber and logs and spur tracks. Across the middle of the sheet runs the Delaware River Bridge, drawn as an anchorage and approach with footways, with the piers and docks of the river front on either side. A large dock and lumber piles occupy the left of the sheet, and the river is lettered at the left edge. Railroad tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad run along Delaware Avenue. A compass rose is drawn at the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with the street grid turned about 14 degrees from true north. Adjoining sheets are 46 above, 35 above right, 29 to the right and 48 below.
notes: The previous-edition sheet number is cut off in the binding gutter.

Placed by a three-point fit on Delaware Avenue at Vine, Elm and Linden Streets, hand-picked at the street centre (60 ft street, centre taken half the width from the drawn edge, not the off-centre water pipe); all three lie along one street, so the placement is a helmert fit.

Delaware Avenue north of the bridge approach has been rebuilt; the Ben Franklin Bridge (drawn here as the Delaware River Bridge) and its plaza cut across the area, and the lumber yards and mills are gone.
printed sheet 47, 50 ft: lumber yards and Delaware River Bridge crossing; three points on Delaware Av, low confidence

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 shows the Camden riverfront industrial strip between the Delaware River on the left and Delaware Avenue on the right, from the Linden Street end of the Reading Railway's freight yards at the top down to Cooper Street at the bottom, with Penn Street crossing the middle of the sheet. The two large blocks are occupied by the Campbell Soup Company and, between them and the avenue, the J. Ervenson and Sons soap factory. The soap works fills the upper block with the grease house, boiler house, soap powder, glycerine, kettle house, laundry soap and toilet soap departments, and beside it the Campbell Soup Company's Warehouse No. 4 and, further left, the long yellow Warehouse No. 5 reach out over the river edge. South of Penn Street the Campbell Soup Company's Mutual Risk buildings, Warehouses No. 2, 3 and 6 and a pulp department, stand against Delaware Avenue. Across the top of the sheet the Philadelphia and Reading Railway freight yards carry many tracks, coal trestles and a Linden Street Freight Station with long sheds, and a loop of sidings curves around the soap works and runs down the whole sheet. Penn and Cooper Streets are drawn as wide, unbuilt rights of way with only the water pipes in them. The river at the left is shown in blue with a pier outline, and the compass rose sits in it. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 14 degrees from true north; adjoining sheets are 47 above, 49 below and 29 and 21 to the right.
notes: Printed sheet number 48, previous edition sheet 3 of volume 1.
The printed street names are 'DELAWARE AV.', 'LINDEN ST.', 'PENN' and 'COOPER'; modern names are Delaware Avenue, Linden Street, Penn Street and Cooper Street.

The detector found only the Delaware Avenue junctions, with tracks in the avenue confusing the edges; all three junctions on Delaware Avenue (Linden, Penn, Cooper) were hand-picked at the street centres.
The west ends of Penn and Cooper Streets and the whole waterfront have been filled and rebuilt since 1926 and were not used as control.
printed sheet 48, 50 ft: Campbell Soup / Ervenson works, Reading freight yards; three points on Delaware Av, low confidence

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers the waterfront below Cooper Street down to the Pennsylvania Railroad ferry terminal at Market and Federal Streets, with the Delaware River along the left edge and Delaware Avenue cut off by the right edge. The top half belongs to the Victor Talking Machine Company: the power house with its coal bunkers and I.E.P. boiler section at the left, then the grinding plant, the record manufacturing building and the long dry kilns, all fireproof construction, with a core plant below them and a yard office at the right. A note under Cooper Street says admittance was refused and the survey was made from plans, with a reference to sheet 21. Below the Victor works a band of Pennsylvania Railroad tracks crosses the sheet, and under it the P.R.R. ferry boat repair shops with a machine shop, print shop, blacksmith shop, a ticket shed and two filling stations. A diagonal driveway to the ferries runs from the lower left up to the right, lined on its south side with a row of small shops and a bakery with portable ovens, and beyond it lies a curved plaza at the foot of Market Street. At the bottom left the P.R.R. terminal and ferry with waiting rooms, express, baggage and office buildings stands over the river, and the P.R.R. repair shops with coal pile, tin shop, carpenter shop and wood working stand above it. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 14 degrees from true north; sheet 48 adjoins above and sheet 50 below.
notes: The left edge of the scan cuts off part of the printed sheet number, so the sheet number is read as 49 from the neighbouring sheets' references.

Delaware Avenue is cut off by the right edge of the scan: its centre line lies at or just beyond the image edge, so the Cooper Street and Delaware Avenue junction is hand-picked with the avenue centre estimated 60 ft from its drawn west edge.
The curved plaza and the diagonal driveway to the ferries do not follow the modern Market Street; the Market and Delaware junction was not used as control.
The Victor Talking Machine Company works and the ferry terminal no longer exist.
printed sheet 49, 50 ft: Victor works and PRR ferry terminal; anchored on Cooper / Delaware, low confidence

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows the Pennsylvania Railroad's Camden terminal and shops, between the Delaware River at the left and South 2nd Street at the right, from Federal Street at the top to Clinton Street at the bottom. The upper left is occupied by the train shed of the ferry and rail terminal, with the electric trains platforms, a power house and a stock building, and the many tracks fan out from it across the sheet. The Pennsylvania Railroad Company terminal shops and ferries fill the centre with a very large open area marked full of tracks, with a freight transport shed and ferry slips on the river side, water tanks, a coal bin and an oil house in the middle, and at the bottom an engine house in the form of a round house with a turn table. Armstrong and Latta dock builders have a storage and repair shop at the bottom left. Along South 2nd Street at the right stand the Penna R.R. freight station with its long platforms, and above it a few dwellings and shops near Mickle Street. Above the tracks, small blocks between Federal Street and Taylor Avenue hold the Pennsylvania Railroad offices at South Front Street. The street edges are drawn only along the right side and top; the yard has no street lines. The compass shows north up the sheet, and adjoining sheets are 49 to the left, 15 above, 16 and 9 to the right and 51 below.
notes: Printed sheet number 50, previous edition sheet 1-5 of volume 1 (printed '(1-5 Vol. 1)').
The sheet is drawn at 100 ft to an inch; the fit is about 1.4 percent below the atlas constant for that scale.
'WASHINGTON' is cut by the right edge of the scan; the printed suffix is not visible.

Most of the streets on the right edge (Mickle, Stevens, Benson, Washington, Berkley, Senate) no longer exist as such: only Clinton Street and the southern part of South 2nd Street survive in OpenStreetMap.

Placed by a two-point helmert from the Clinton Street and South 2nd Street junction and a pipe crossing at Federal and South Front Streets carried from sheet 15; the junction of Federal Street and Delaware Avenue, picked separately, agrees to about 1.4 m.
printed sheet 50, 100 ft to an inch: PRR terminal, shops and ferries, Federal St to Berkley St along S 2nd St

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 is the southern edge of Volume One, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, and is almost entirely empty ground. Clinton Street crosses the sheet near the top, 50 feet wide, with a single building, a general contractor's storage shed of the J. E. Brenneman Company, on the large vacant lot below it at the left near the river shore. A Pennsylvania Railroad line runs down South Front Street, a narrow street with two tracks, and divides the empty river-side area from a strip of building lots on its east side, where a few lot lines are drawn between South Front Street and Spring Street. Peach Street slants across the lower right, 40 feet wide, and Spring Street runs down the right edge at 20 feet. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked in Clinton Street and the compass rose sits in the blank area at the upper left. A line of text at the bottom, See Camden Volume Three, shows that the ground below belongs to another volume, and the left edge carries part of the river shoreline. Adjoining sheets are 50 above.
notes: Printed sheet number 51, previous edition sheet 30 of volume 2 (the number is partly cut by the left edge of the scan).
Blank ground below Clinton Street at the left carries the note See Camden Volume Three.

Placed only from block corners at Clinton Street, South Front Street and Spring Street carried from sheet 50; no modern junction is drawn here, so the rest of the sheet is extrapolated from the top edge.
The text along the left edge (river shoreline) could not be read.
printed sheet 51, 50 ft: nearly blank, Clinton to Peach; carried from sheet 50, low confidence
